title: Hipparcos primary eclipses of CO Eri occur about one hour after the TESS linear ephemeris
abstract: We test Hipparcos eclipse times before the ASAS-3 and TESS timing surveys. Position matching gives ten Hipparcos sources among 304 tested binaries. CO Eri is the only one with a prior common-mode period change. Its 96 good Hipparcos transits place the primary eclipse 65.1 minutes after the TESS ephemeris at effective year 1991.89, with a conditional fit error of 2.9 minutes and a further TESS extrapolation error near 5.1 minutes. A free template width and a separate symmetric shape agree. One-point deletion gives 64.0 to 67.5 minutes. Model variants show larger errors than the formal fit. The secondary is too poorly sampled for an independent common-mode shift. A circular timing model fitted to 61 Hipparcos, ASAS-3, Gaia and TESS measurements has period about 18.8 years and chi-square 51.44 for 54 degrees of freedom, against 123.01 for a constant period derivative. But an extra five-minute Gaia error admits short-period aliases near three years; ten minutes changes the best branch. CO Eri has a historical semi-detached classification. We report an independent early eclipse-clock measurement, not a confirmed third star or a secure outer period. The package gives code, full likelihood profiles, failed fits, source hashes, shape tests and a separate-scratch reproduction script.

display.caption: Hipparcos CO Eri primary timing under three shape models, tested fixed-template variants and mission halves, and the weak secondary profile.
Four-survey timing measurements and conditional circular and drift fits. The period scans show the role of the Gaia epoch. The 18.8-year branch is not a secure orbit.
